newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China hits out at HK over visit by dissident.
newsitem.headline: China hits out at HK over visit by dissident.

text.p: China has hit out at the Hong Kong government for allowing a visit by Chinese dissident Chai Ling and warned it against turning the territory into a base for subversives, a newspaper reported on Tuesday.

The warning, from the Xinhua news agency in Hong Kong, China's de facto embassy in the territory, referred to a visit by Chai, one of the student leaders who spearheaded the 1989 democracy movement in Beijing's Tiananmen Square.

"The Chinese side requests that the Hong Kong government honours its commitment of having no intention of turning Hong Kong into a subversion base or a venue for political struggles," the South China Morning Post quoted a Xinhua spokesman saying.
Chai, 28, flew into the territory from the United States over the weekend on a private visit.
The self-exiled dissident, who is studying for a master's degree at Harvard University, was given a one-week visa by the Hong Kong government.
On Monday, she gave a news conference where she voiced concerns over the future of freedoms in Hong Kong after it is handed back to China at midnight this June 30.
But she also said she was optimistic of China's future and hoped ultimately to return to her country to work.
The Hong Kong government has chosen to stay silent.
"We have no comment on individual cases of visa applications," a government spokeswoman said.
